task_truth.truth_description: y = x . w_star + nonlinearity_scale * (mean_j cos(x_j) - exp(-1/2)) + noise, with per-row noise sigma depending on the latent margin |x . w_star|. The latent truth (latent_teacher_score, latent_signal, noise, regime) is recorded but is never an input to training or to the online diagnosis.

known_optimum.note: w_star is the known optimum of the linear part; the small cosine term keeps the task from being a purely separable linear demo

leakage_probe.note: z-scoring with all-rows statistics shifts each feature mean by at most 0.06736; the published pipeline fits on the fit rows only so no evaluation row influences the transform

preprocessing.note: evaluation rows are held out of every fitted statistic; the rows themselves stay in the published task so the two sides can be inspected

reproducibility.note: the two same-seed runs agree on the data hash; the different-seed run is recorded to show that the hash is seed-sensitive

incidents.description: loss creeps down, then compounds at ~13.5% per step; the online call made at step 36 is divergence_risk, and the run is confirmed diverged afterwards
a slow mode stalls the loss on a plateau from ~step 18 to ~step 50, then the same run descends again; the correct online call is wait_for_transient
this single seeded curve looks like a clean win; the paired-seed audit in seed_audit reverses its sign, so the curve alone cannot support the claim
the prefix contains both an escalation and a subsequent fall, so the online detector abstains instead of inventing a winner
the prefix is flat within its own noise floor; the online detector reports unresolved rather than a direction

incident_bank.diagnosis_protocol: diagnose_online() is called with exactly the telemetry points whose step is <= decision_step; the stored telemetry_inputs are that same prefix, and the detector raises if any hidden-truth key is present in its input

trace_generation.note: each trace is a deterministic seeded synthetic training trace

config.pairing: same data, same initial weights and the same minibatch index schedule for both arms on a given seed; only the arm configuration differs
config.interval: normal-approximation 95% interval for the paired mean difference (project choice; no paired-seed power calculation is performed)

single_seed.claim: seed 0 alone puts arm B 0.0057 (0.52%) above arm A, so that seed's winner is A
single_seed.why_misleading: one seed gives a direction that does not survive the paired sweep

best_of_n.claim: best-of-3 runs: arm A reaches 1.0276 at seed 2, 0.47% below arm B, so A wins
best_of_n.why_misleading: best-of-N rewards the luckiest seed and hides the seed-to-seed spread; the paired interval still includes zero

eyeballed_curve.claim: the first 80 steps look cleaner for arm A (median loss 1.1110 against 1.2450, 10.76% lower), so that schedule is the better one
eyeballed_curve.why_misleading: the early transient is a burn-in effect, not a converged comparison; the arms cross later and the paired result does not replicate the early ranking

seed_aware_summary.claim: paired over 8 seeds, the mean difference in the mean_training_loss_over_last_20_steps between arm B and arm A is -0.0030 (95% interval [-0.0252, +0.0192]; 4 seeds favour B, 4 favour A); with no paired-seed power calculation the comparison is unresolved and no winner is certified
seed_aware_summary.status_reason: the paired differences change sign across seeds and the interval includes zero

seed_audit.note: every declared seed is reported; no seed was dropped after seeing its result

incident_accounting.note: abstain and unresolved are reported as their own outcomes; they are excluded from the accuracy denominator instead of being scored as correct or incorrect
